chunks: And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Three things impose the state of Ihram: Talbiyah (verbal declaration), Al-Ish'ar (shaking the garment), and Al-Taqlid (tying the garment). If one performs any one of these three, he has entered the state of Ihram.

key_terms.التَّقْلِيدُ: Tying the garment (specifically the upper garment) to signify Ihram
key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةُ: The verbal declaration of 'Labbayk' (Here I am)
key_terms.الْإِحْرَامُ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْإِشْعَارُ: Shaking the garment to signify entering Ihram

ai.seo_question: What actions are required to enter the state of Ihram in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the practical legal triggers for entering the state of Ihram, emphasizing that the obligation is activated by the performance of any one of three specific actions: verbal declaration (Talbiyah), shaking the garment (Al-Ish'ar), or tying the garment (Al-Taqlid). In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the principle that the physical or verbal act of assuming the ritual state, rather than a specific prior intention alone, constitutes the binding entry into Ihram. This ruling underscores the importance of immediate compliance with ritual purity and restrictions once the pilgrim engages in these defining acts.
